correctness.rationale: Exact orthogonal diagonalization gives the radial Rayleigh quotient. Euler integral makes the nonterminating hypergeometric factor a positive Beta(m,n/2) expectation. Uniform fractional-moment bounds of m(1-V) yield Gamma(n/2,1) convergence and an integrable majorant e^{-u}u^alpha(1+u)^{n-2} for all alpha>-1. Fixed T<1 gives uniform numerator convergence and a one-sided endpoint Laplace estimate. The denominator scales as m^{-(alpha+n-1)}; the resulting eigenvalue powers alpha+n-2 and alpha are checked against the n=4 known integer benchmark. The eventual spectral-degree ordering follows from positive T^m times powers. Exact spherical-harmonic multiplicities and spectral threshold inversion provide the claimed coefficient and O-error. The standalone finite checker completed 98 assertions; it is only supplementary.

value.rationale: The object is the natural radial concentration compression on a weighted hyperbolic-harmonic Bergman space, compared at identical geometry and weight to Euclidean-harmonic concentration. The first spectral-count difference is a new parameter-independent log-log law with dimension-dependent order and sharp coefficient. Odd-dimensional radial hypergeometric factors do not terminate, and the Beta-Gamma boundary-layer argument is a substantive structural bridge. Counts measure how many independent harmonic modes retain prescribed subball mass; the result is relevant to concentration and approximation, beyond a routine scalar normalization or isolated finite calculation.
